### Contributing guidelines

- [x] I have read [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] I have updated 'mini.nvim' to latest version of the `main` branch

### Module(s)

mini.surround

### Neovim version

0.11.x

### Description

Hi! 2 days ago a [commit](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/commit/fbb6ad02871d296fc7d3ebd453e1be89b1210f68) to the surround module was made, I wonder if my previous setup "is supported"? Just wanted to share my edge case basically

From my time with some other surround plugins I got used to the mapping:

```
mappings = {
	add = 's',
	-- ...
},
```

So typing `siw)` would add a surrounding to a word. I find surrounding so much useful than the builtin `s`, so I don't mind remapping it

But now the `s` seems to be mapped to `<Nop>` with my configuration. Is this expected?

### Reproduction

1. Create separate 'nvim-repro' config directory:
    - '~/.config/nvim-repro/' on Unix
    - '~/AppData/Local/nvim-repro/' on Windows

2. Inside 'nvim-repro' directory create a file named 'init.lua'.
   Populate it with the following content:

    ```lua
    -- Clone latest 'mini.nvim' (requires Git CLI installed)
    vim.cmd('echo "Installing `mini.nvim`" | redraw')
    local mini_path = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site/pack/deps/start/mini.nvim'
    local clone_cmd = { 'git', 'clone', '--depth=1', 'https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim', mini_path }
    vim.fn.system(clone_cmd)
    vim.cmd('echo "`mini.nvim` is installed" | redraw')

    -- Make sure 'mini.nvim' is available
    vim.cmd('packadd mini.nvim')
    require('mini.deps').setup()

    require('mini.surround').setup {
		n_lines = 20,
		respect_selection_type = true,
		search_method = 'cover_or_next',
		silent = true,
		highlight_duration = 500,
		mappings = {
			add = 's',
			delete = 'ds',
			replace = 'cs',
			find = 'sn',
			find_left = 'sN',
			highlight = '',
			suffix_last = '',
			suffix_next = '',
			update_n_lines = '',
		},
		custom_surroundings = nil,
    }
    ```

3. Run `NVIM_APPNAME=nvim-repro nvim` (i.e. execute `nvim` with `NVIM_APPNAME` environment variable set to "nvim-repro").
   Wait for all dependencies to install.

4. Try pressing `s`
   - Expected: `add` action
   - Actual: `<Nop>`

5. Try `siw)`
   - Expected: `add` around current word with `()`
   - Actual: `s` is noop, `iw)` inserts raw `w)`

<details><summary>What to do after reporting an issue</summary>

After reporting the issue, it is safe (and even recommended for cleaner possible future bug reports) to remove 'nvim-repro' config from the system:
- Delete config directory ('~/.config/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete data directory ('~/.local/share/nvim-repro' on Unix).
- Delete state directory ('~/.local/state/nvim-repro' on Unix).

</details>

comment_data.body:
It looks like this commit fbb6ad02871d296fc7d3ebd453e1be89b1210f68 noops for `s` even when no mapping starts with s. I use the default `s` behaviour to delete char under cursor and enter insert mode. It no longer works on the mentioned commit.

Config to repro

```lua
require('mini.surround').setup({
    mappings = {
        add = 'ys',
        delete = 'ds',
        replace = 'cs',
        find = '',
        highlight = '',
        update_n_lines = '',
        suffix_last = '',
        suffix_next = '',
    },
})
```

Thanks for the issue!

It was an oversight on my part. Didn't account for this use case. Should be fixed on latest `main`. Sorry for troubles!

---

> Config to repro

@antonk52 It is because this doesn't fully follow the [recommended way](https://nvim-mini.org/mini.nvim/doc/mini-surround.html#minisurround-vim-surround-config) of setting up 'vim-surround' like style of mappings. It misses `find_left`, which means that `sF` mapping is still created. Usually this leads to the delay of 1 second (`:h 'timeoutlen'`) before executing the built-in `s` key.

Following the suggested approach of setting these mappings doesn't override `s`. And I personally would suggest using `cl` for such cases.

title: [mini.surround] mapping `add` to just `s` no longer works
